Posterior probability of each observed categorical cell's own level

Source: R/cellgloc_categorical.R
dot-gloc_cat_prob_observed.Rd

For every observed categorical cell: the probability of the level it holds, computed as if the cell were missing, at the returned fit and without a refit. A miscoded cell whose continuous cells point elsewhere gets a small value. Other missing categorical cells of the row enter through the row's pseudo-rows. The estimation does not use this value.

.gloc_cat_prob_observed(
  X,
  M,
  W,
  B,
  Sigma,
  catp,
  priors,
  design,
  es,
  w_min = 0.5,
  band = .gloc_peer_band
)

Arguments

X, M, W, B, Sigma

the continuous data, mask, weights and returned fit.

catp

result of .gloc_cat_prepare.

priors

result of .gloc_cat_fit_priors.

design

one-sided formula.

es

the last E-step (or .gloc_cat_identity).

w_min, band

the peer rule.

Value

an \(n x k\) matrix, NA where the cell is missing and in every column of a row above the combination cap, which has no pseudo-rows to compute it from.

Details

The density is evaluated at the row's expected design row rather than averaged over its level combinations – a Jensen approximation, taken because the pseudo-rows are already weighted. It is exact for a row whose other categorical cells (every categorical variable except v, the column being computed) are all observed. Corrected: an earlier version of this paragraph said that is every row whenever only one categorical variable has missing cells, for every column v. That is false for any v other than the one variable with missing cells: computing that other, fully observed variable's column still hits the approximation on any row where the one variable with missing cells is itself missing. The exact case is only v's own column, and only because "only one variable has missing cells" then means every other variable has none, anywhere.
